lesson_title: The Boxes That Were Never Real
hook_text: Any two people on earth share about 99.9 percent of their DNA, so why did South Africa spend decades sorting people into boxes?
clip_script: Pick any two people on the planet. Their DNA is about 99.9 percent the same. Skin colour is just the body adjusting to sunlight over thousands of years. So where did the idea of superior races come from? It grew alongside slavery and colonialism, an excuse to treat people as property and take their land. Later, bad science measured skulls to prove the lie. The Nazis took it to genocide. After the war, scientists rejected it. But in 1948, South Africa wrote it into law. Your box decided your home, your school, your job and your vote. That is institutional racism. The laws are gone, but the scoreboard is still uneven. Racism is learnt. Which means it can be unlearnt.
visual_style: A DNA double helix; a map of world skin tones shading gradually; an old engraving of a slave ship; a nineteenth-century skull chart crossed out; an apartheid identity document showing a race classification; a diverse group of learners in a classroom today.
pacing: Quick facts at the start, slower and firmer at apartheid, uplifting at the end.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to understand what racism is and how it can be challenged.
